oneLiner: Custom AI accelerators and Ethernet switching for six frontier-model builders, with VMware software funding the build. The market is betting that the two-year doubling outlook is a peak financed by Broadcom's own guarantees rather than a contracted ramp; the stock works if FY2027 simply lands near the guide.
thesis: Contracted demand, not a forecast. Remaining performance obligations were $179.2B in the Q3 FY2026 10-Q (about 25% due within 12 months), and Anthropic's amended S-1 lists Broadcom as its largest compute counterparty at $161B (both via TIKR); the gigawatt schedule behind the outlook is named customer by customer.

The largest 2027 customer just funded itself. Anthropic priced its IPO on Nov 18, 2026 at $83, above the $70-78 range, selling about 980M shares for roughly $81.3B alongside a $26B private placement - the counterparty the market worried about most now holds the cash for its 2027 lease payments.

Networking is paid whoever wins the socket. AI networking grew 2.5x YoY in Q3 FY2026 and was 27% of AI revenue; Tomahawk 6 is described as nearly sold out and Tomahawk 7 (200 Tbps) has taped out, so a share shift between accelerator designers does not remove Broadcom from the rack.

Software and cash conversion carry the balance sheet. Infrastructure software runs at 94% gross margin, trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow is $49.4B on capex of 1.5% of revenue, and $5.6B of debt was repaid in Q3 FY2026 plus $1.5B after quarter-end.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 FY2026 (ended Aug 2, 2026; reported Sep 2, 2026)
points: AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY and +54% QoQ, 56% of revenue; XPUs 73% of AI revenue.
Non-GAAP gross margin 75.0% (GAAP 69.1%); non-GAAP operating margin 67.9% (GAAP 53.9%).
Non-GAAP EPS $3.32 (+96%) on 4.94B diluted shares; GAAP EPS $2.68.
Free cash flow $13.67B, 46% of revenue; capex $532M; no buybacks in the quarter ($8.45B in the nine months).
Balance sheet at Aug 2, 2026: cash $24.0B, total debt $59.4B (4% weighted coupon, 7.4-year average maturity).

segments: Semiconductor solutions 70% of Q3 FY2026 revenue (57% a year earlier): custom XPUs, Tomahawk AI networking, PCIe switching, optical DSPs and lasers, wireless, broadband, storage. Non-AI semiconductors were $4.2B, +5% YoY and flat QoQ.
Infrastructure software 30%: VMware, mainframe, security. ARR +15%; VMware Private AI Cloud is the enterprise-AI attach and the workload-repatriation pitch.
competitive: NVIDIA remains the pricing umbrella: its Q3 FY2027 (reported Nov 17, 2026) revenue was $115.8B with a $130B Q4 guide. Broadcom claims an XPU co-designed to one lab's workload matches Rubin-class GPUs at less than half the cost (management claim, unverified).

MediaTek is the live threat inside Google: it designs the TPU 8t series, and a Nov 20, 2026 supply-chain report says Google is moving 2027 volume toward it. Marvell competes for other co-design sockets.
Physical constraints bind before commercial ones: substrates, leading-edge wafers, HBM and customer land, power and shells. Broadcom plans its own Singapore substrate fab in FY2027.
VMware alternatives (Nutanix, Proxmox, hyperscaler-native) still circle the installed base, but software growth says the repricing is holding.
moat: Multi-generation co-design contracts lock in customers years ahead of revenue. Per the Sep 2, 2026 call: Google at multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually; Anthropic 1GW in 2026, another 5GW of TPU v8i in 2027 and line of sight to an incremental 10GW in 2028; OpenAI 1.3GW in 2027 and over 5GW in 2028; Meta 3GW through 2028 - about 30GW across six customers, not all of it inside the period. Underneath sit SerDes, packaging and memory-integration IP and Ethernet switching leadership.
risks: Two pre-profit labs carry the outlook. Management expects Anthropic to be the largest XPU customer in 2027 and OpenAI the second largest in 2028; Rothschild and Co Redburn downgraded to Neutral on Nov 13, 2026, arguing both must become self-financing 'in short order', and Anthropic's amended S-1 showed Q3 compute costs growing faster than revenue (via TIKR).

Broadcom is underwriting its own demand. The $35B AI XPV tranche (June 2026) carries a backstop of up to about $29B, and the $63B Anthropic SPV (8-K dated Oct 26, 2026) adds residual value support equal to the first-lien portion, reported at about $43.5B (Reuters via Finimize; unverified against the filing). Together that would exceed the company's total debt, and it is off balance sheet.

Google can re-source a generation. TF International's Ming-Chi Kuo reported on Nov 20, 2026 that Google cut planned 2027 TPU 8i shipments by about 1M units, roughly 20%, mostly the higher-priced 8i Max, in favour of MediaTek-designed TPU 8t; neither company has confirmed it.

Gross margin is diluting as systems and memory content rise. Non-GAAP gross margin went from 78% in Q4 FY2025 to a ~73% guide for Q4 FY2026; the GAAP operating margin expansion the filings show (49% to 54%) rests on opex leverage that ends when revenue growth slows.

The price needs a decade, not two years. The page's reverse DCF requires about +14.8% a year of free-cash-flow growth for 10 years against +7.4% a year of revenue growth over the last three fiscal years; the current run rate clears it easily, a post-FY2028 digestion does not, and customer land, power and permitting decide which (see debate 4).
catalysts: Dec 9, 2026: Q4 FY2026 and full-year results after the close - FY2027 AI outlook, Google's 2027 plans, Q1 gross margin, total backstop exposure (debates 1, 2, 3).

Late Jan to early Feb 2027: Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon Q4 calls with 2027 capex figures; Alphabet said on Oct 28, 2026 that 2027 capex 'will increase significantly' without a number (debates 2, 4).
Q1 2027 (date unconfirmed): Anthropic's first quarterly report as a public company - revenue growth vs compute cost (debate 1).
Early Mar 2027 (date unconfirmed): Q1 FY2027 results - first quarter of deliveries under the $63B Anthropic SPV and the gross-margin floor test (debates 1, 3).
Jan to Mar 2027: state legislative sessions where data-center construction moratoriums were campaigned on (debate 4).

valPresets.note: Growth presets are year-1 rates that fade to terminal. The bear preset (15%) is roughly the constant rate the reverse DCF says is priced in; the base preset (40% fading) is consistent with FY2027 AI revenue landing a little below the ~$115B outlook.

latestProse: Q3 FY2026 (ended Aug 2; reported Sep 2) remains the latest print; Q4 is not out until Dec 9, 2026. Revenue of $29.59B beat the $29.4B guide, with AI semiconductors $16.7B and XPU shipments up 3.5x YoY. The disclosure that matters: non-GAAP gross margin fell 210bp sequentially to 75.0% while non-GAAP operating margin hit a record 67.9% - memory and system content dilute cost of goods as warned, and operating leverage offsets it for now. Net debt is about $35B against quarterly free cash flow of $13.67B, so the reported balance sheet is not the issue; the contingent guarantees are (risk 2).
guidanceProse: Q4 FY2026 guide: revenue about $34.8B (+93% YoY), AI semiconductors $21.7B (+236%), software about $8.7B (+25%), non-AI semiconductors about $4.3B, gross margin about 73%, operating margin about 66%, non-GAAP tax rate about 16%, 4.94B diluted shares. FY2026 AI revenue lands near $58B. The outlook, as worded on the call: 'secured the supply to again double AI revenue to approximately $115 billion' in FY2027, demand 'exceeds this outlook', 'line of sight' to $230B in FY2028 with supply secured, and 'very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028' (non-GAAP basis implied, not stated). What moved the stock since: the in-line guide (Sep 3); the $63B Anthropic SPV with a Broadcom backstop (Oct 26), which revived vendor-financing worries; a 10.4% drop on Nov 5 in a post-midterm chip selloff on reported data-center moratorium pledges, with no company news; a relief rally after Nvidia's CEO resigned on Nov 12; the Redburn downgrade (Nov 13, -7%); and an 11-12% drop on Nov 20 on the unconfirmed Google report, on a day the semiconductor index fell 8%. Nvidia's Nov 17 print, which raised its FY2028 growth framework to ~75% from ~70%, says end demand is intact; the selling is about who pays and who supplies.

verdict.summary: The stock has been marked down as if the FY2027 outlook were already cut, while the only hard data since the print - Nvidia's raised growth framework and Anthropic's IPO proceeds - points the other way. Our base case sits about 9% below the $115B AI outlook and about 12% below consensus FY2027 EPS and still supports a higher value; the bear case needs both a funding failure at the labs and a Google share loss. The asymmetry is positive but the bear case is deep, because Broadcom has guaranteed the leases that buy its own chips. Two things would change the view: a cut to the FY2027 AI outlook on Dec 9, or backstop exposure growing faster than AI revenue.
wtb: FY2027 (year ending about Oct 31, 2027) AI semiconductor revenue reaches at least $105B against the ~$115B outlook, starting with a Q1 FY2027 AI guide at or above about $24B on Dec 9, 2026.
Non-GAAP gross margin settles at or above 70% in FY2027 and operating margin stays at or above 65%, so net margin holds near 54%.
Anthropic and OpenAI fund 2027 deployments without Broadcom's residual-value support rising above about $75B in total by the Q1 FY2027 report (early Mar 2027).
At end-2027 the market pays about 21x FY2027 non-GAAP EPS, which only requires FY2028 to grow about 40%, not double.

bear.why: AI revenue reaches only ~$85B: Google moves a generation toward MediaTek, lab deployments slip a year on power, permitting and funding, and SPV tranches stop clearing without larger guarantees. Operating margin falls to ~62% as mix dilutes and leverage fades (net margin 51%). FY2028 looks flat, so the market pays a peak-cycle multiple and discounts the contingent liabilities.

base.why: AI revenue ~$105B (a Google trim and site delays cost ~$10B of the outlook), software ~$36B, non-AI semiconductors ~$17B; operating margin ~65.5%, net margin 54%. FY2028 is seen growing ~40% rather than doubling, so 21x FY2027 is about 15x FY2028 EPS - below the five-year average forward multiple of 24x (TIKR), reflecting customer concentration.

bull.why: The outlook is beaten: AI revenue ~$120B as demand above supply converts, the Google report proves wrong or small, and operating margin holds ~68% (net margin 56.5%). The $230B FY2028 outlook and EPS above $30 stay credible, so 26x FY2027 is only about 16-17x FY2028 EPS, and public-market funding at Anthropic removes the counterparty discount.

scenarioModel.note: EPS basis is non-GAAP diluted (the basis of management's FY2028 target and of consensus, which was $19.47 for FY2027 from 48 analysts on Nov 13, 2026); GAAP EPS runs about 20% lower (Q3 FY2026: $2.68 vs $3.32) because of acquisition amortization and stock compensation. EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / 4.95B diluted shares: bear 137 x 51% = $69.9B = $14.1; base 158 x 54% = $85.3B = $17.2; bull 174 x 56.5% = $98.3B = $19.9. Net margin = (operating margin less ~1.2-1.5 points of net interest) x (1 - 16% tax). FY2026 base is ~$105.9B (Q1 $19.31B + Q2 $22.19B + Q3 $29.59B + Q4 guide $34.8B). Multiples are applied to FY2027 EPS at end-2027. Inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Can Anthropic and OpenAI pay for the gigawatts they have ordered?
debates.bull: Anthropic has just raised about $81.3B in its IPO plus a $26B placement, the leases are financed by banks, Apollo and Blackstone rather than by Broadcom, and the guarantees are dual-trigger: a default and a shortfall in chip resale value.
debates.bear: Neither lab is self-financing; the WSJ reported the $63B deal needed the CEO's intervention to close (via Constellation Research), and Broadcom reportedly bought $1B of Anthropic IPO shares (24/7 Wall St; unverified) - a supplier guaranteeing and funding its customer.
debates.view: Funded for FY2027, open for FY2028. The IPO moves Anthropic's 5GW from hope to cash, so we underwrite the FY2027 outlook at a ~9% haircut but give the $230B figure little credit in the base multiple.

signpost.metric: FY2027 AI revenue outlook and disclosed maximum residual-value exposure
signpost.threshold: positive if ~$115B is reiterated with exposure quantified below ~$75B; negative if the outlook is cut below $105B or exposure is not disclosed

debates.q: Is Google dual-sourcing away from Broadcom?
debates.bull: On Sep 2 management said the Google engagement 'has never been stronger' and that it shipped TPU v8i ahead of MediaTek's part; Kuo himself attributes the cut to tight supply and data-center power, not a design loss, and Anthropic's TPU volume runs through Broadcom.
debates.bear: A ~20% cut concentrated in the highest-priced part is exactly how share loss starts, and Google has every reason to cultivate a cheaper second designer for inference.
debates.view: Treat the report as roughly right until denied: it is in our base case as part of the ~$10B shortfall to the outlook. One trimmed generation does not break the thesis; a second supplier taking the next generation's lead part would.

signpost.metric: Management comment on Google 2027 TPU volume; Alphabet 2027 capex guide
signpost.threshold: positive if Google TPU revenue is guided up YoY in FY2027 and Alphabet capex rises 30%+; negative if Broadcom concedes share on the next generation
signpost.when: Dec 9, 2026 call; Alphabet Q4 call, early Feb 2027

debates.q: Does operating margin hold while gross margin falls?
debates.bull: Opex is about 6% of semiconductor revenue; in Q3 FY2026 operating margin rose 240bp YoY while gross margin fell, and management asks investors to judge operating margin.
debates.bear: Rack-scale sales with pass-through memory can take gross margin below 70%, the Q4 guide already steps operating margin down to ~66%, and leverage disappears the quarter growth slows.
debates.view: Margin dilution is real but priced: every point of operating margin is about $0.27 of base-case EPS, small next to the revenue debate. It becomes a thesis issue only if operating margin breaks 63%.

signpost.metric: Q1 FY2027 guide: non-GAAP gross margin and operating margin
signpost.threshold: gross margin at or above 71% and operating margin at or above 65% holds the base case; below 70% and 63% moves toward the bear case
signpost.when: Dec 9, 2026 guide; confirmed in the Q1 FY2027 report, early Mar 2027

debates.q: Is FY2028 the peak the reverse DCF cannot afford?
debates.bull: The outlook is supply-limited with demand above it, about 30GW is contracted across six customers, and Nvidia has just raised its own next-year growth framework.
debates.bear: The +14.8% a year of free-cash-flow growth priced in for a decade is double the trailing three-year revenue growth rate; newly elected governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia reportedly campaigned on data-center moratoriums (Motley Fool via Trefis; unverified), and management itself says FY2028 depends on customer sites being ready.
debates.view: The amber flag is fair but backward-looking: trailing free cash flow of $47.9B roughly doubles by FY2027 in our base case, which covers most of the decade's required growth early. We do not pay for $230B; we need FY2028 to be up, not double.

signpost.metric: FY2028 AI outlook and combined 2027 hyperscaler capex guidance
signpost.threshold: positive if $230B is reiterated and 2027 capex is guided up 25%+; negative if FY2028 is reframed as dependent on sites not yet permitted
signpost.when: Dec 9, 2026; hyperscaler Q4 calls, late Jan to early Feb 2027
